video_directives: Diagram cards (180 dB gauge, pain zone, 36,000 lives) each hold ~3s with eased fade-ins — keep this exact hold cadence
Character reacts to every beat (dizzy, clutching ears, shocked, somber) — sustain pose/emotion swaps between scenes to preserve life
The gauge-to-ear dissolve and BOOM ripple expansion are motivated, breathing transitions — extend this eased dissolve language; avoid any snap-cuts

top3_directives: The third line 'WAS AN ISLAND' drops to a dark gray that nearly merges with the navy ocean band — raise its brightness or switch to the cream white used on lines 1-2 so the full title reads at a glance.
The mascot character's arm and leg overlap the 'T' and 'H' of 'THE LOUDEST' — nudge the character left/up 20-30px or add a soft dark halo behind it to separate it from the type.
The lower-third ocean band is a large near-black dead zone between the shoreline and the text block; enlarge the type ~15% or lift the ocean with subtle wave-line highlights to reclaim that area.
Trim hook to ≤6 words (e.g. 'THE LOUDEST SOUND EVER' + visual implies island) to hit the 8+ text tier
Upper third is a near-empty star field — extend smoke rings or add a subtle moon/arc detail to occupy the dead zone
Text block sits low with heavy bottom weight — nudge composition upward ~5% and add a faint glow/rim on the title for separation from the water band
Brighten the third line 'WAS AN ISLAND' — it reads visibly dimmer than lines 1-2 and drops legibility in daylight
Fill the upper ~25% dead zone (above the green arc) with a subtle element — moon, birds, or star cluster — to earn the vertical space
Nudge the title block up 3-4% to reduce crowding against the bottom frame edge and rebalance the volcano-to-text ratio
JAVA/SUMATRA labels are muddy mid-gray on dark navy — brighten to near-white or add subtle glow; they will vanish on a daylight phone screen
Bottom third is a dead zone: the glow-outlined character is small, dim, and disconnected from the volcano focal point — enlarge/integrate it or cut it and extend the wave detail upward
The repeating tan water-line dashes read as unfinished placeholder bars — either style them as actual wave highlights (varying width, opacity) or remove them
The word 'AGAIN.' is nearly invisible — dark cream fill on dark navy background at the very bottom; brighten it to match the main caption or delete it
Remove the faint horizontal underline bars above/behind the text and the stray dark ellipse shapes floating above the volcano tip — they read as rendering artifacts
Mascot character overlaps the left edge awkwardly and faces the text but isn't anchored to anything; either ground it with a shadow/ledge or nudge it fully into frame

The bottom third is a dead zone: the stick-figure character is tiny and dim — enlarge it 2-3x or cut it, and give 'PRESSURE WAVE' a real title treatment (bolder weight, brighter fill) so the lower frame carries weight
'PRESSURE WAVE' fails daylight contrast — it is low-opacity gray on near-black navy; raise to ~85% white or a brand accent color with subtle glow
Add a subtle drop shadow or dark halo behind the '180 dB' pill and gauge numerals so they separate cleanly from the bright purple gradient bleeding behind them
The sound-wave arc floats detached to the right of the ear with no connection point — anchor it emanating from the ear canal or remove it
Bottom third is a murky near-black dead zone with a tiny illegible character — either enlarge/brighten the figure into the composition or crop the frame to end at the horizon
Two disconnected text systems ('PAIN ZONE' label + '130 dB = PAIN' pill) split attention — merge into one badge or place both in a single aligned block
Brighten the 'EARDRUMS SPLIT' caption — light gray on mid-purple will mush on a daylight phone; push to near-white with a subtle dark halo
The character bottom-left is tiny and low-contrast against the near-black water — either enlarge ~30%, add rim light, or remove it; right now it reads as noise
The lower third is a large dead zone of flat dark navy — add faint water-surface glow reflection from the purple sky or subtle wave highlights to unify the composition
Add a subtle dark scrim or lift the character's rim light — bottom-left figure currently sits near legibility floor on small screens
Break the large dark dead zone in the top 40% with faint star parallax or a thin atmospheric gradient accent
Unify the caption chip styling (border radius/color) with the arc palette so the two text systems read as one family
Fill the bottom-third dead zone: the mascot floats in near-black emptiness — anchor it with subtle ground glow or a faint orbital echo curve so the lower frame isn't a void
Add a thin dark rim/stroke between planet and the purple nebula glow on the right edge — the teal atmosphere line nearly melts into the highlight there
Give the caption pill a touch more presence (slight scale-up or drop shadow) so the single text system commands the frame instead of reading as an afterthought
Boost the '36,000 LIVES' badge contrast or remove it entirely — as rendered it's a ghost element that reads as a rendering error, not a design choice
The character bottom-right is almost invisible against the navy ground; raise its brightness, scale, or rim light so it reads as the focal subject at 6 inches in daylight

Kill the dead zones: top ~55% of the frame is empty gradient and the bottom third is featureless navy — either add atmospheric layers (stars, mist, horizon glow) or reposition text/character to occupy the mid-band with intent
Remove or merge the two overlapping circles (orange + teal) — they read as UI artifacts and split the focal point with the volcano; keep at most one highlight ring
Boost contrast of the 'GONE.' label — grey text on glowing purple is the weakest element on a 6-inch daylight screen; use white with a subtle dark scrim or heavier weight
Give the small character a clear role — at bottom-left it's nearly invisible against dark water; either enlarge, rim-light it, or cut it to clean up the composition
The 'CHILD OF KRAKATOA' subtitle is nearly invisible — muted teal on dark purple; brighten it, add a subtle drop shadow, or place it inside the pill card
The bottom-quarter horizontal lines read as unresolved placeholder text — either render real captions with proper contrast or remove them; right now they're dead mush against the navy background
The character bottom-left is dim, small, and disconnected from the composition — lift it with a rim light or reposition it into the eye path between the volcano glow and the caption zone
Boost separation of the foreground character from the dark shoreline — add rim light or glow so it survives a 6-inch daylight screen
Activate the bottom third: the wave lines and faint dashes read as dead zones; add a subtle reflection of the beacon light on the water
Strengthen the eye path between the small character and the beacon — a subtle light beam or scale adjustment connects the two focal points
